rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE: server.py defines two parallel data structures — MODULES list (line 137-158) and MODULE_FEATURES dict (line 166-259). The granular feature catalog (MODULE_FEATURES) includes `invoices_created` with 6 feature keys, but the master MODULES list never includes a top-level entry with key=`invoices_created`. Consequence chain: (1) MODULE_KEYS = [m['key'] for m in MODULES] is missing 'invoices_created'; (2) GET /api/rbac/module-features iterates `for m in MODULES` so the response omits invoices_created entirely (19 modules instead of 20); (3) POST/PUT /api/users normalizer line 3282 / 3328: `if mk not in MODULE_KEYS: continue` silently drops any invoices_created entries from incoming payloads; (4) frontend Users.js accordion is data-driven by the catalog response → no row rendered for invoices_created; (5) admin auto-seed `all_features_dict()` iterates MODULE_FEATURES.items() so the admin gets a seeded invoices_created.* = True dict, but no other user can ever receive it. REPRODUCTION: GET /api/rbac/module-features → response has 19 modules; POST /api/users with `permission_actions: {invoices_created: {cancel: true}}` → response shows no `invoices_created` key in the created user's permission_actions; visually open the Edit User modal in /arc/users → accordion shows 19 rows, footer reads `X dari 19 modul aktif`, no row labeled `Invoice Tercetak`. MITIGATION: Add `{'key': 'invoices_created', 'label': 'Invoice Tercetak', 'default_roles': ['finance']}` to the MODULES list (one-line change), and ideally add a startup assertion `assert set(MODULE_FEATURES.keys()) == set(MODULE_KEYS)` to prevent future drift.
